q15:
I like consulting because it lets me work on real problems with the people who own them, and see the result change something. Procurement appeals to me because the impact is so concrete. Every organisation spends a large share of its money with suppliers, so better decisions there show up directly in cost, quality and sustainability, and the results can be measured.

Most of my experience so far has been close to this kind of work, even if it was not called procurement. At DS Digital Technology, a pharmaceutical client needed a clear way to judge AI models for a patient-facing service. I worked with their clinical experts to agree the criteria, built a 246-question benchmark and a scoring rubric, and compared six models across more than 2,400 responses. The client adopted it as their acceptance standard. That project felt a lot like a supplier evaluation: define what good looks like with the stakeholders, compare the options fairly, then make a clear recommendation.

At Ipsos Strategy3 I built market-sizing and forecasting models and turned more than 80 expert interviews into data for client reports, and at TikTok Shop UK I build KPI frameworks and dashboards that commercial and operations teams use to track performance.

Procurement consulting would let me use these skills, analysing spend and data, building a fact base and working with stakeholders, on problems with a clear commercial outcome. I also like that it touches almost every industry, so I would keep learning how different businesses work. In the long term I would like to become a consultant who can both find the opportunity in the numbers and help a client actually deliver it.
q16:
Three things stood out to me about Proxima.

The first is the practitioner approach. Proxima's consultants work side by side with clients and take responsibility for results, rather than handing over a report and leaving. The graduate role also says it is "not a passive learning role", and that is what I want. In my internships the most valuable moments were when I had to make something work in practice, for example building an AI agent with Claude Code at TikTok Shop UK to automate a campaign configuration task that my team had been doing by hand, which cut the time it took by around 40 to 50 percent.

The second is the focus on measurable outcomes. Proxima works across cost, capability and sustainability, and talks about value that clients can see. I like work where the result can be measured, because it keeps the analysis honest.

The third is the breadth. Proxima works across sectors from healthcare and life sciences to retail, energy and financial services, and as part of Bain & Company it works with very large organisations. With my background in health data and consulting projects for healthcare clients at Ipsos Strategy3, I would be keen to contribute to healthcare and life sciences work, but I am also excited to learn sectors I have not worked in yet.

I was also drawn to the structure of the graduate programme, especially the case study programme and the regular presentation practice. Communicating findings clearly to non-technical audiences is something I work on all the time, and I would value the coaching.
q17:
I think I would be a good fit because I combine strong analytical skills with real experience of working with clients and making changes happen.

I have an MSc in Health Data Science from UCL, where a distinction is expected, and a BSc in Biological Sciences from Imperial. My dissertation used data from 458,840 UK Biobank participants, so I am comfortable working with large, messy datasets and checking that a result holds up before I present it. I use Excel, SQL, Python and PowerPoint regularly.

I have also worked in client-facing roles. At Ipsos Strategy3 I worked on consulting projects for healthcare clients, building market-sizing and forecasting models and turning expert interviews into structured data. At DS Digital Technology I worked directly with a pharmaceutical client's clinical experts to agree evaluation criteria for an AI service and presented the results and recommendations to their clinical and business teams. At TikTok Shop UK I build KPI frameworks and dashboards for operations and commercial teams, and I look for ways to make processes faster, like the AI agent I built to automate a manual configuration task.

A few things about me outside work: I enjoy learning new tools as soon as they come out and often build small side projects to try them, such as a question-answering agent over NHS health pages. I also love being outdoors, which is how I reset and think more clearly. At Imperial I volunteered with the Natural History Museum's urban nature programme and was an Undergraduate Wellbeing Representative, and I led a team supporting more than 20,000 attendees at HUAWEI Connect in Shanghai.

I am organised, curious and happy to take responsibility early, which I think suits Proxima's approach.
